propositions: Repository-isolation autouse guard teardown probes timeout at fixed five-second watchdog during full-suite concurrent execution despite passing in isolated/sequential runs.
Instrumented measurement shows probe latency p99=2.08s and max=3.30s under 18-process concurrent load, but only p99=67ms and max=507ms sequentially, never reaching five seconds in any controlled arm.

Shared-host oversubscription with one-minute load p50=76.4 and peak 170, combined with process count max=771 and sampled CPU p50=1,614%, correlates with slow probe execution and one explicit fork-failure OSError.

The five-second watchdog contract from callous-amused-hart is calibrated to bound hung child processes; observational evidence did not detect any successful probe exceeding five seconds, rejecting the need to raise the timeout.

Runtime evidence rules out PATH contamination, Git-environment pollution, monkeypatched Git, test-local state, and insufficient process-creation delay as root causes; scheduler/filesystem starvation on overloaded host is the confirmed mechanism.
